title: 2001 HMMT February Team Problem 1
statement: How many digits are in the base two representation of 10 ! (factorial)?

solutions.text: We write \(10!=2^{8} \cdot 3^{4} \cdot 5^{2} \cdot 7\). The number of digits (base 2 ) of 10 ! is equal to \(\left[\log _{2} 10!\right]=8+\log _{2}\left(3^{4} \cdot 5^{2} \cdot 7\right)\). Since \(2^{1} 3<3^{2} \cdot 5^{2} \cdot 7<2^{1} 4\), the number of digits is \(8+13=\) 21.
